name: Dev-Team Agent With a Dedicated Selector Routing to Exactly One Specialist (Strategy.ROUTER)
query: Our dev-team agent has three specialists — `planner`, `coder` and `reviewer` — and every request should go to exactly one of them, no back-and-forth between them. I don't want the specialists deciding; I want a small, cheap classifier making the call. Python. How would you set this up, and what has to be running in prod?
expected_behavior: Step 1: Consult references/agent-sdks.md §6 (the `router` row: a dedicated classifier — an `Agent` or a Python callable — picks exactly one child; no shared conversation; a callable `router` is a worker that `serve()` registers), references/agents.md §3/§4, references/optimization.md F1/F3, and WebFetch the Python SDK `docs/agents/` before pinning the install (Rule 7.3).
Step 2: Three specialists with unique names, `provider/model`, their own `instructions`, `@tool`s and `max_turns`: `planner`, `coder`, `reviewer`.

Step 3: A dedicated selector that is NOT one of the specialists: `selector = Agent(name="selector", model="openai/gpt-4o-mini", instructions="Reply with exactly one of: planner, coder, reviewer.", max_turns=1)`; then `team = Agent(name="dev_team", model="openai/gpt-4o-mini", agents=[planner, coder, reviewer], strategy=Strategy.ROUTER, router=selector)`.

Step 4: Offer the callable alternative: `def pick(prompt: str) -> str: ...` returning a child name, passed as `router=pick` — cheaper and deterministic — and state that a callable router is a worker `serve()` registers, so the agent worker gate (Rule 9) applies to it as well.

Step 5: Semantics: exactly one child runs per request; there is no shared conversation between children (contrast with HANDOFF, where control transfers mid-conversation, and SWARM); the result is the chosen child's output. Children compile to `SUB_WORKFLOW`s.

Step 6: Lifecycle: `runtime.run(team, prompt)` locally under `if __name__ == "__main__":`; `runtime.plan(team)` to see `requiredWorkers` (the specialists' `@tool` workers plus the callable router if used); `runtime.deploy(team)` in CI; a long-lived `runtime.serve(team)`. Never `conductor deploy`.
Step 7: Optional workflow invocation: `AGENT` with `agentType: "conductor"`, `name: "dev_team"`, `prompt`, `maxDurationSeconds`; never `agentType: "router"`.

Step 8: Tests: `mock_run(team, "Implement the login endpoint", events=[...])` with `expect(result).handoff_to("coder")` / `assert_agent_ran("coder")`, and `validate_strategy` (raises `StrategyViolation`) to check the routing shape.
success_criteria: The router is a separate `Agent` (or a Python callable) passed as `router=`, and is not one of `planner` / `coder` / `reviewer`
The parent uses `strategy=Strategy.ROUTER` (or `"router"`) with `agents=[planner, coder, reviewer]`
States that exactly one child runs per request and that there is no shared conversation between the children (contrasted with handoff/swarm)
Each specialist and the selector have unique `name`s and their own `max_turns` (the selector bounded to a single turn or similar)
States that a callable `router` is a worker registered by `serve()` (worker gate applies), and names the process that serves the specialists' `@tool` workers
Any `AGENT` task uses `agentType: "conductor"` + `name: "dev_team"` — never `agentType: "router"` or a framework name
Does not hand-wire the routing as a workflow `SWITCH` plus three `AGENT` tasks as the primary solution (mentioning it as an alternative is fine)
